note: Both sets repeat the same facts many times (pipe diameter, bolt diameter, angle size, and plate thicknesses appear 2–4 times each) and both use the vague entity "structural element" for the 1'-8" and 1'-4 1/4" dimensions. Set A reads the values cleanly (3" pipe, 3/4" bolts, 1"/1/2"/3/8" plates, L3x3x1/4 angle, 4 X 3/8" cap plate), with only one unsupported claim (the bare 1/4" bound as "Crane Attachment Detail thickness/gap") and it omits the PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 plate. Set B does capture that plate, but six of its claims stuff label text into the value field ("3 DIA STD. PIPE", "3 DIA", "1/2 PL TYP", "3/8 PL TYP", "1 PL TYP", "3/4 DIA"), and one quote ("1\" PL") is truncated so it no longer supports the "typical" condition. On balance A is the more faithful set despite its one misbinding and its missing plate claim.
remarks: Both extractions are heavily duplicated: the same callout is re-emitted under several entity spellings (pipe/bolts/plate/angle), so 18-25 'claims' cover roughly 8 distinct facts. Both sets also miss the T.O. STEEL 11'-4" elevation and the small 3/8" dimension shown in the detail. Set B's recurring failure mode is copying the whole callout string (e.g. '3/8" PL TYP') into the value field instead of parsing the numeric value and unit; Set A's is binding bare dimension fragments (1/4") to the detail as a whole.
